name: Moba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Kantchoa, Laré 2005. Description de la langue moba: approche synchronique (long grammar, Univ. de Lomé); Prost & Digoë 1961 Grammaire moba; neither online

sources.citation: Pike, Kenneth L. 1982. Tune and tone: generalized syntagmatic pitch patterns constrained by particular lexical patterns. JWAL 12(2): 22-41 (sect. IV uses Jann Russell's Moba data).
sources.note: Moba: 'Four phonemic levels of tone seem verified'; tone-sandhi matrices. The stress discussion in the paper concerns other languages, not Moba.

sources.citation: Mindri, Nakane; Pouguinimpo, Yambame; Roberts, David; Boone, Carin. 2022. Vers une orthographe appropriée du ton pour le moba. Lomé/Cotonou: SIL Togo-Bénin.
sources.note: Most recent SIL treatment of Moba prosody (tone orthography experiment); likely summarises the tone system and any stress/accent facts relevant to reading.

sources.citation: ATAPEB. [2015]. Alphabet moba-ben (2-page chart).

Koabike, Bedouma. 2012 [1st ed. 2006, provisional ed. 2005]. Cours de grammaire et d'orthographe moba (pour les lettrés en français). 2e édition. Dapaong: ATAPEB. 56 pp. (= Glottolog ref 106687; Ben dialect)
sources.note: Nothing. p.5 'Le moba est une langue à ton'; p.51 three tones (haut, moyen, bas), contextual realisations, tone not. The word 'accent' does not occur in the document.

sources.citation: Peace Corps Togo. 2010. Moba O.P.L. Workbook. (livelingua.com)
sources.note: p.2 'The moba language is tonal and uses at least three main tones: High, medium, Low.' No mention of stress (a full-text search for stress/accent = 0).

sources.citation: Koabike, Bedouma. 2005 [1995]. Parler Moba 1 (cours de leçons moba). 2e éd. Dapaong: ATAPEB. 62 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; conversational lessons, no pronunciation section.

sources.citation: Rialland, Annie. 1985. Le fini/l'infini ou l'affirmation/l'interrogation en moba (langue voltaïque parlée au Nord-Togo). Studies in African Linguistics, Supplement 9: 258-261.
sources.note: Melody is reserved for tone ('4 tons et downstep'); statement/question marked by abrupt vs gradual voice offset and final-vowel lengthening. Nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: Prost, André. 1967. Le Moba. Dakar: Université de Dakar, Documents linguistiques [no. 11?]. 73 pp. (supersedes Prost & Digoë 1961 Grammaire moba)

sources.note: Google Books shows a hit for 'accent' on p.10 inside the tone section (pp. 9-10) but withholds the snippet; Prost's Voltaic sketches typically include a one-line 'accent' statement.

sources.citation: Kantchoa, Laré. 2005. Description de la langue moba: approche synchronique. Thèse de doctorat, Université de Lomé. ix+667 pp. (and Kantchoa 1994, Description phonologique du moba, mémoire de maîtrise, Lomé, xiv+140 pp.)

sources.note: Largest modern description (Glottolog's top-ranked grammar); its phonology part (building on the 1994 phonology MA) should state whether Moba has an accent in addition to tone.

sources.citation: Russell, Jann M. 1985. Moba phonology. MA (Hons) thesis, Macquarie University, Sydney. xiv+214 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open link recorded by Glottolog or the catalog, not checked
sources.note: The only full phonology of Moba in English by an SIL fieldworker; an SIL-style phonology write-up normally has an explicit stress/rhythm section alongside tone. Most likely to contain a first-hand stress statement.

sources.citation: Rialland, Annie. 1983. Le système tonal du moba comparé à celui du gurma. In J. Kaye, H. Koopman, D. Sportiche & A. Dugas (eds), Current Approaches to African Linguistics, vol. 2, 217-234. Dordrecht: Foris (De Gruyter reprint).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The principal published tonology of Moba (4 tones + downstep); would confirm authoritatively that the prosodic system is purely tonal (full-text search suggests the word 'accent' never occurs in the chapter).
